mechanism_narrative: Persistent negative RETAIL_REC across all four weeks (range -20.0 to -25.6) indicates a structural suppression of discretionary mobility. This suppression will continue into the next four weeks absent a shock, keeping RETAIL_REC negative relative to baseline and lower than the current mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC has remained between -20.0 and -25.6 for four consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the mean of the last 28 days by more than 2 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has stabilized at approximately -28 percent over the last three weeks, signaling that commuting constraints are no longer deteriorating. This stabilization removes a downward pressure on retail foot traffic, allowing RETAIL_REC to recover modestly upward over the next four weeks as behavioral adaptation to transit constraints reaches equilibrium.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-on-week change magnitude falls below 1 percentage point
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -31.0 (t-3w) to -26.1 (t-2w) to -28.1 (t-1w) to -28.0 (t-0w)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines by more than 3 percentage points in the next two weeks, or TRANSIT falls below -30 percent.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has remained stable near -21 percent across four weeks without further deterioration. If workplace restrictions remain unchanged (no new tightening), retail-and-recreation venues will experience a predictable baseline of foot traffic from the non-working population, stabilizing RETAIL_REC near current levels rather than declining further.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES does not fall more than 2 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES range is -20.9 to -23.9 across four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -15 percent in the next four weeks, or WORKPLACES falls below -25 percent.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility shows high volatility (ranging from -17.3 to +2.3 percent) while RETAIL_REC remains consistently suppressed. When PARKS mobility is positive or near-zero, it indicates outdoor activity substitution is active. This substitution effect competes with retail-and-recreation venues, suppressing RETAIL_REC. If PARKS remains negative in the next period, retail venues will capture more discretionary mobility, lifting RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -10 percent for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS was +2.3 at t-2w while RETAIL_REC was -20.0
failure_condition: PARKS rises above 0 percent while RETAIL_REC remains below -22 percent in the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has stabilized at approximately -3 to -6 percent, indicating essential shopping patterns are resilient and predictable. This stability in essential mobility anchors household routine patterns. When essential mobility is stable, discretionary retail-and-recreation mobility tends to follow a similar stabilization trajectory rather than deteriorate further, producing a floor effect that prevents RETAIL_REC from declining below current levels.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM range is -5.9 to -2.0 across four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the last 28-day mean by more than 3 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has remained elevated and stable at 8.4 to 10.0 percent across all four weeks, indicating sustained home-based activity. High residential mobility combined with suppressed RETAIL_REC suggests a strong substitution effect: people are spending time at home rather than in retail venues. This substitution pattern will persist into the next four weeks, keeping RETAIL_REC suppressed relative to baseline.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is 8.4-10.0 while RETAIL_REC is -20.0 to -25.6
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL falls below 5 percent while RETAIL_REC rises above -15 percent in the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are both suppressed at approximately -28 and -21 percent respectively, indicating coordinated reduction in commuting and workplace presence. When both commuting and workplace activity are jointly suppressed, the retail-and-recreation sector loses the weekday foot traffic from commuters and workers. Recovery in RETAIL_REC requires simultaneous recovery in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES; if either remains suppressed, RETAIL_REC will not recover significantly.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below -20 percent
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is -26.1 to -31.0 and WORKPLACES is -20.9 to -23.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -18 percent in the next four weeks while either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES remains below -20 percent.

mechanism_narrative: April 15 marks mid-autumn in Sydney with seasonal transition effects on outdoor mobility patterns. PARKS volatility (t-2w: +2.3 percent) suggests seasonal outdoor activity is emerging. If seasonal outdoor preference strengthens over the next four weeks, PARKS will rise further, drawing discretionary mobility away from indoor retail venues and suppressing RETAIL_REC relative to baseline expectations for this period.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above 0 percent for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS reached +2.3 at t-2w, indicating seasonal outdoor preference emergence
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -18 percent while PARKS remains below -5 percent over the next four weeks.
